The main takeaway from our work is that
the X-ray data are very difficult to interpret in the framework of standard hot spot models.
the X-ray data are consistent with the hot spots being the result of shocks propagating into a relatively low density environment (n ~ 10-4 cm-3) with a relatively low magnetic field (B ~ 1-3 μG).
the X-ray data, when combined with the radio, optical, and infrared data, provide a wealth of information about the physical conditions in the jets and lobes.
